priority: You primarily work on documents — drawings, PDFs, email. Almost any current computer handles that, so the monitor matters more than the computer.

AutoCAD runs one operation at a time, so a fast CPU core matters more than many — though almost any current chip drafts smoothly. Drawings with many xrefs and nested blocks want more RAM and fast storage. The monitor matters more than the computer.

Modeling runs one operation at a time — what counts is how fast each CPU core is, not how many. That's what makes Revit, Rhino, and SketchUp feel responsive. Get a modest dedicated GPU for stable viewports. More powerful ones are only needed for visualization.

Real-time visualization renders on the GPU — Enscape, Lumion, D5, and Twinmotion draw the scene live as you move. A more powerful card renders faster, and VRAM sets how large a scene you can hold. The CPU only matters for loading.
These tasks need two things at once — a fast CPU core for modeling and a powerful GPU for visualization. Neither can be cheap, so expect to pay more than for either alone.

Final rendering in V-Ray or Corona runs on your CPU cores — it uses every one at once, so the number of cores sets your render times. More cores, faster renders. AMD's Ryzen 9 leads, and Threadripper PRO goes further on a dedicated render box. GPU rendering keeps improving, so it's worth a look if you're still CPU-only.
